correctness.rationale: The group law gives the standard alternating commutator form. For each nonzero quotient vector, conjugation varies the central coordinate through a nonzero linear functional, hence through the entire field, so noncentral classes are exactly the q-element fibers indexed by nonzero symplectic vectors. Adjacency is therefore orthogonality. The projective-line partition proves the clique blow-up; dimensions of orthogonal intersections prove degree, diameter, clique bound, and common-neighbor formulas. The spectrum follows from the inspected projective symplectic spectrum and the explicit lexicographic-product eigenvalue transform. The packaged replay independently checks all structural claims in five finite cases.

value.rationale: The theorem gives a complete structural and spectral description for a standard infinite class-two group family, extending the same-graph spectral program beyond the center-index-p^2 and metacyclic cases in the closest literature. Its symplectic realization yields exact diameter and maximum clique size and exposes a qualitative field-size transition: strong regularity at q=2 versus two adjacent common-neighbor types for every q>2.
